title: M Pizza Ordering Platform
tagline: An Arabic-first pizza ordering system with customer app, staff web and live order tracking.
problem: A pizza business needed one connected flow for customers, staff and delivery updates instead of disconnected ordering and fulfilment tools.

process.title: Product flow
process.text: Mapped the customer ordering journey, staff workflow and live order states around the needs of an Arabic-first product.

process.title: Interface
process.text: Designed a clear mobile ordering experience and a focused staff workspace with status-driven interactions.

process.title: Build
process.text: Implemented a Flutter customer app with a Node.js TypeScript Fastify API, PostgreSQL and staff web tooling.

result: The repository contains a connected ordering platform foundation covering customer ordering, staff operations and live tracking.

title: Nawa Bilingual RTL Landing Page
tagline: A bilingual landing experience designed for Arabic-first communication and accessible direction switching.
problem: A bilingual product needs more than translated strings: hierarchy, alignment, navigation and focus behavior must remain clear in both directions.

process.title: Structure
process.text: Organized the landing page around a concise value proposition, proof points and clear conversion paths.

process.title: RTL system
process.text: Built the layout and content structure to support Arabic RTL alongside English without duplicating the page.

process.title: Build
process.text: Implemented the responsive interface with React, TypeScript and Vite, with accessibility considered in the interaction model.

result: A polished bilingual landing page is available for review with a clear responsive structure and RTL-aware presentation.

title: Landing Lab: Three UX/UI Directions
tagline: A frontend exploration of three distinct landing-page directions for comparing hierarchy, tone and conversion flow.
problem: Choosing a landing direction is difficult when visual style, content hierarchy and interaction decisions are mixed together in one unstructured draft.

process.title: Explore
process.text: Created three focused directions so typography, spacing, tone and content emphasis could be compared side by side.

process.title: Refine
process.text: Kept the information architecture consistent while varying visual language and interaction details.

process.title: Build
process.text: Implemented the explorations as a responsive React and TypeScript site with reusable layout patterns.

result: The project turns early design exploration into a browsable comparison that makes direction selection easier to discuss.

title: FitnessTracker SwiftUI Health App
tagline: A privacy-first offline iOS fitness tracker with health metrics, goals, charts and a home-screen widget.
role: iOS product design and SwiftUI development
problem: People need a focused way to understand workouts and progress without sending personal health data to a remote service.

process.title: Information
process.text: Structured a daily dashboard around Apple Health metrics, workouts, goals, streaks and progress trends.

process.title: Accessibility
process.text: Included English and Arabic RTL considerations, VoiceOver support, reminders and a widget-oriented glanceable view.

process.title: Architecture
process.text: Designed a Swift 6 and SwiftUI foundation using SwiftData, HealthKit, Swift Charts, WidgetKit and a simplified Clean Architecture.

result: The public repository documents a privacy-first iOS product direction and its planned app, tests and widget targets for macOS implementation.

title: Modern E-Commerce Storefront
tagline: A responsive storefront with product browsing, categories, promotional sections and cart interactions.
problem: A product catalogue needs to make browsing, category discovery and shopping actions feel simple across screen sizes.

process.title: Structure
process.text: Organized navigation, category sections, a promotional hero and product cards into a clear browsing flow.

process.title: Interaction
process.text: Added shopping actions and data-driven product presentation so the interface feels like a usable storefront rather than a static mockup.

process.title: Build
process.text: Implemented the responsive frontend with HTML, CSS, JavaScript and JSON data.

result: A live responsive storefront demonstrates the core browsing and shopping interaction patterns in a lightweight frontend.
